counterbalancing: Question order is reproducibly shuffled per repetition. Pair order alternates per question; across the even-sized primary cohort, each arm appears first equally often in every repetition.

questions.query: Where is the number of directory traversal workers chosen?

facts: HiArgs selects one thread for sorted output or one explicit file, otherwise it honors an explicit count or uses available parallelism capped at 12.
The selected count is passed to WalkBuilder::threads for parallel traversal.

questions.query: Which code decides whether hidden files are skipped?

facts: WalkBuilder::hidden configures hidden-file filtering, and HiArgs enables that filtering unless --hidden was requested.
Incremental ignore matching applies hidden filtering after ignore rules, so an explicit whitelist match can take precedence.

questions.query: Where is searching stopped after encountering binary data?

facts: SearcherBuilder stores the binary-detection policy and Searcher can update the line buffer with it.
The search core records the first configured binary byte and stops when the policy is Quit; Convert reports binary data but continues.

questions.query: Where does the program decide between streaming a file and mapping it into memory?

facts: Searcher tries the configured memory-map strategy for path searches and otherwise uses the generic streaming reader.
Memory-map feasibility is platform/configuration dependent, and a failed optional map falls back to ordinary reading.

questions.query: Where are external programs selected to read compressed files?

facts: DecompressionMatcherBuilder compiles default and custom path-glob associations, with later associations taking precedence.
The search worker asks that matcher for a path's command and wraps the file in DecompressionReader when a command matches.

questions.query: How are rules from parent ignore files combined with local rules?

facts: The root matcher loads the parent ignore chain before adding rules for the root directory.
Traversal derives child matchers from their parent, caching the chain and layering each directory's local ignore rules on top.

questions.query: Where are input bytes converted from another character encoding before matching?

facts: SearcherBuilder configures DecodeReaderBytesBuilder with the selected encoding and BOM policy.
search_reader wraps the input in that decoder before either multiline or line-oriented matching.

questions.query: Where does case sensitivity depend on whether the pattern has capital letters?

facts: Smart case selects case-insensitive matching only when a literal exists and the pattern contains no uppercase literal.
An explicit case-insensitive choice wins, while disabled smart case leaves matching case sensitive.

questions.query: Where is context around matching lines assembled for output?

facts: The search core retains the configured number of preceding lines and tracks visited lines so it can emit before and after context around matches.
Discontiguous context groups are signaled to the sink, where a printer can render a separator.

questions.query: Where is an unsupported regular expression retried with the alternative engine?

facts: EngineChoice::Auto first builds the Rust matcher and returns it when successful.
Only after the Rust build fails does it try PCRE2; if both fail, it reports both compilation errors.

questions.query: How does RegexMatcherBuilder build one matcher from several patterns?

facts: build delegates one pattern to build_many, while build_many treats all patterns as one alternation.
It builds the configured HIR, applies whole-line or word wrapping, compiles the regex, and derives a literal prefilter where possible.

questions.query: Where does SearcherBuilder configure treatment of binary input?

facts: SearcherBuilder::binary_detection stores a BinaryDetection strategy in the searcher configuration.
The strategy controls both which byte marks binary data and whether the search quits or converts the detection into a report.

questions.query: How can WalkBuilder be told to follow symbolic links?

facts: Call WalkBuilder::follow_links(true); the default is false.
The stored flag is passed into serial or parallel traversal, which follows symlinks while guarding against loops.

questions.query: Where does GlobBuilder turn a wildcard pattern into a parsed glob?

facts: GlobBuilder::new stores the pattern and default options without compiling it.
build creates a Parser, parses wildcard tokens, validates alternates, and returns a Glob with its regex and tokens.

questions.query: How does TypesBuilder select the file types that will be searched?

facts: select marks named type definitions for inclusion and negate marks definitions for exclusion before build compiles their globs.
When at least one type is selected, paths not matching a selected type are ignored; negated matches are also ignored.

questions.query: Where can StandardBuilder change the separator between context groups?

facts: StandardBuilder::separator_context replaces the optional separator bytes; the default is -- and None disables it.
The standard printer writes the configured separator between discontiguous context groups.

questions.query: How does JSONBuilder produce a sink for structured match events?

facts: JSONBuilder::build creates a JSON printer with cloned configuration and a counting writer.
JSON::sink or sink_with_path binds a matcher and optional path into JSONSink, which emits begin, match/context, and end messages.

questions.query: Where does DecompressionMatcherBuilder obtain its default command associations?

facts: Defaults are enabled on the builder, and build chains default_decompression_commands with custom associations.
The default loader finds installed decompressor executables and registers their known extension globs, skipping unavailable programs.

questions.query: How does parse_reader treat comments and empty lines in a ripgrep config file?

facts: parse_reader trims each line, skips empty lines and lines whose first non-space character is #, and treats every remaining line as one full argument.
A bad line is recorded as an error without discarding valid arguments from other lines.

questions.query: How does search_parallel create and run the search workers?

facts: search_parallel creates one configured SearchWorker and clones it once per parallel walker worker.
Each directory result becomes a Haystack, is searched, contributes match/statistics state, and its buffered output is printed; errors continue and broken pipes quit.

questions.query: What should I put in a config file so every search uses my preferred options?

facts: Set RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH to the desired file; ripgrep does not search a standard config location automatically.
Put one complete shell argument on each trimmed line, use leading # for comments, and do not use shell escaping; explicit CLI flags come later and normally override config flags.

questions.query: Which documented options let one match span several input lines?

facts: Use -U or --multiline to permit matches and reported results that span multiple input lines.

questions.query: What does the documentation recommend when I need look-around or backreferences?

facts: The default finite-state regex engine does not support lookaround or backreferences.
Use the optional PCRE2 engine with -P/--pcre2; the installed build must have PCRE2 support.

questions.query: How do I search a file whose text is encoded differently from UTF-8?

facts: Pass -E/--encoding with a WHATWG encoding label; ripgrep transcodes files from that encoding unless a BOM supplies the encoding.
Automatic mode detects UTF-16 BOMs, while -E none disables transcoding and BOM sniffing and searches raw bytes.

questions.query: Where are the instructions for installing ripgrep or building it from source?

facts: README.md's Installation section links precompiled release archives and lists platform package-manager commands.
The same section documents cargo install ripgrep and cargo binstall ripgrep for Rust-based installation.

questions.query: How do command-line glob overrides get from parsed options to directory filtering?

facts: HiArgs builds an Override with the working-directory root, adds --glob values and case-insensitive --iglob values, then passes it to WalkBuilder::overrides.
The override matcher applies whitelist and ignore glob precedence while the walker filters each path.

questions.query: How does selecting JSON output connect CLI configuration to match-event serialization?

facts: HiArgs::printer_json transfers CLI printer settings into JSONBuilder and builds the JSON printer selected for JSON search mode.
That printer creates a JSONSink whose begin, matched/context, and finish callbacks serialize one structured JSON message per event.

questions.query: How do options read from a config file reach the normal command-line parser?

facts: config::args reads RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH and turns the file into one argument per non-comment line.
parse_low first detects whether config is enabled, prepends those config arguments to the real CLI arguments, then runs the normal parser again so later CLI flags can override them.

questions.query: How does a directory entry found by the parallel walker become a searchable input?

facts: The parallel-walker callback passes each traversal result to HaystackBuilder::build_from_result.
HaystackBuilder logs traversal errors, accepts explicit inputs or file entries, rejects other entries, and returns the Haystack consumed by SearchWorker::search.

questions.query: How does a chosen character encoding reach the reader that supplies bytes to the matcher?

facts: HiArgs maps an explicit encoding to SearcherBuilder::encoding, leaves Auto at its default, or disables BOM sniffing for Disabled.
SearcherBuilder configures its decode reader, and search_reader wraps the source with that decoder before matching.

questions.query: Where does ripgrep turn non-printable path bytes into escaped display text?

facts: grep_cli::escape converts tabs, carriage returns, newlines, non-printable ASCII, and invalid UTF-8 bytes into readable escape sequences; escape_os applies it to OS strings.

questions.query: How can a caller collect total bytes searched and matches produced?

facts: Enable or obtain a printer Stats value and read bytes_searched() and matches(); one printer's Stats covers all searches executed with that printer.
Stats values support Add and AddAssign for aggregation across printers or searches.

questions.query: follow symbolic links

facts: WalkBuilder::follow_links(true) enables following symbolic links during traversal; false is the default.

questions.query: configuration file

facts: The guide says to set RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH and put one complete argument on each trimmed non-comment line; ripgrep does not auto-discover a config path.

questions.query: Where does ripgrep store user login sessions?

facts: It does not: ripgrep is a local line-oriented recursive search tool, and this repository contains no application login-session storage subsystem.

questions.query: Which ripgrep module submits credit-card payments to a checkout service?

facts: None does: ripgrep is a local line-oriented recursive search tool, and this repository has no payment-processing or checkout subsystem.
